name: reveal-stagger
summary: A deck of cards that flies in on scroll, staggered from the last card back, with anime.js' responsive scope switching between a landscape fan and a portrait column.

sync.description: How closely the animation tracks the scrollbar. Upstream's onScroll sync; lower lags further behind the scroll.

enter.description: Where the scroll range starts, relative to the track. Upstream's onScroll enter.

leave.description: Where the scroll range ends, relative to the track. Upstream's onScroll leave.

deviations.what: Selectors are ours (.fx-reveal__card, .fx-reveal__track for upstream's .card and .sticky-container) and the targets are passed as elements rather than as strings.
deviations.why: The example owns its whole page; an effect is one section among several, and a page may carry this one twice. Passing the elements the section actually holds is what keeps two mounts from animating each other's cards.
Same reason. anime resolves a selector string against scope.root, so scoping the root to the section is what makes a second instance on the page independent.

deviations.what: The CSS resting state is the animation's end state, per orientation, rather than the section being blank until the observer fires.
deviations.why: Effect contract: the section has to look finished on CSS alone. A scroll reveal whose observer never runs -- script blocked, bundle pruned -- must not leave the content invisible, so the stylesheet draws the finished deck and the animation is what plays on top.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing is animated and no scroll observer is created.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest, and the resting deck is already the finished content.
